clue.text: Case unfinished in month, needing year to establish pro-women rule

indicators.note: the shortened case sits inside the name of the month

parts.note: March, the third month

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for a court case is not completed

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court

explanation.surface: Someone wants a legal case wrapped up within the month and another year to bring in rule favouring women.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarchy is a social system in which women, especially mothers, hold authority.

clue.text: I am surprised about work without much purpose

indicators.note: the exclamation goes around the abbreviation for work

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone is taken aback by work done aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopy describes a listless, dejected state, drifting without energy or aim.

clue.text: Chief plant-holder, overturned, almost cracked

indicators.note: in a down clue the flowerpot word is turned upside down, reading bottom to top

parts.note: a pot holds a plant

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for crazy is dropped

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, as is cracked

explanation.surface: A plant pot has been knocked over and nearly broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is slang for the leading person or boss in an organisation.

clue.text: I will study team on the left, making the wrong choice?

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to con is to study or pore over
a side is a sporting team
red describes a left-wing politician

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to study a left-wing team, perhaps a poor decision.
explanation.definitionFit: An ill-considered choice is badly thought out; the question mark flags the loose phrasing of the definition.

clue.text: Crime discovered after quantity of money turns up

indicators.note: the wrongdoing word follows the money word

parts.note: a roll is a wad of banknotes
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A crime comes to light once a large sum of cash appears.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll in is to arrive casually, often late, which is to turn up.

clue.text: Applied transfers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: practical, involving direct involvement
second meaning: passes on, as a baton or responsibility

explanation.definitionFit: Hands-on describes practical, applied work, while hands on means passes something along to another person.

clue.text: Number covered by dreadful group

indicators.note: the number abbreviation is enclosed by the word for dreadful

parts.note: bad means dreadful, of poor quality

explanation.surface: A song gets a terrible cover version by a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a musical group, or any company of people acting together.

clue.text: Have nothing to do with criminal injury provided by soldiers

parts.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, an offence in English law
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Someone shuns a violent offence committed by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to detest it and so want no part of it.

clue.text: Failure to limit minor upset for busy German city

indicators.note: the failure word confines the reversed letters within it

parts.note: a dud is something that fails

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for minor is turned over

parts.note: lesser, smaller: less

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling movement, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A failure to keep a minor upset in check in a bustling German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Düsseldorf is a large city on the Rhine, capital of North Rhine-Westphalia.

clue.text: Schoolboy howler not at first recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
the opening letter of the mistake word is dropped

parts.note: a howler is a slip-up, a glaring mistake

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's blunder is remembered in a muddled way.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a child attending school, so a schoolboy is an example.

clue.text: Yearns to be seen around facilities in underwear

indicators.note: the yearning word is placed around the toilet word

parts.note: longs means yearns
john is US slang for a toilet, the facilities

explanation.surface: Someone wants to be spotted near the toilets in their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Long johns are long-legged underpants worn for warmth.

clue.text: Irish writer quick to support king's son

indicators.note: in a down clue the speed word sits underneath, holding up the son's name

parts.note: Jonathan was the son of King Saul in the Bible
swift means quick

explanation.surface: A writer is quick to back a king's son.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, Dublin-born satirist, wrote Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Goes on binge, losing head — wakes

indicators.note: the first letter of the revelling word is removed

parts.note: carouses means drinks and revels

explanation.surface: Someone goes on a bender, loses their head, then wakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Arouses means rouses from sleep, the same as wakes in its transitive sense.

clue.text: Look after new money after dropping penny

indicators.note: the money word appears once its first letter has been shed

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money, such as prize money

explanation.surface: Taking care of new money once a penny has been lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse something is to tend and care for it.

clue.text: Union arrangement ended quiet operation

parts.note: closed means finished
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet operation finished a union deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed shop is a workplace where every employee must belong to a trade union.

clue.text: I feel bad backing lad's affair

indicators.note: the I-feel-ill words are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
to ail is to feel ill
a son is a lad; the 's links it to what follows

explanation.surface: Someone feels guilty supporting a young man's love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship.

clue.text: Celebrity flat is a place for comment?

parts.note: note means fame or distinction
a pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: A star's apartment is a place that invites remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is paper for jotting notes, so somewhere to write remarks.

clue.text: Post Office, suppressing recent failure, compromised image

indicators.note: the post office letters hold down the recent word inside them

parts.note: hot means fresh, just out
a bomb is a flop

explanation.surface: The Post Office hushes up a recent failure that has spoiled its public image.
explanation.definitionFit: To photobomb is to intrude into someone's picture, spoiling it; the definition is read as a verb phrase.

clue.text: Don't come to see comedian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fail to turn up for a date

explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone up is to miss an arranged meeting; a stand-up is a solo comic performing to an audience.

clue.text: Favourite time, tucking into dessert? One could shift some drink

indicators.note: the favourite and time letters go inside the dessert

parts.note: a pie is a pudding
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone's preferred moment is eating pudding, then something to move a drink along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating, but it means placing inside; 'drink' is any liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipette is a laboratory tube used to transfer small measured amounts of liquid.

clue.text: Expression of love involving ultimately playful smack

indicators.note: the love token takes the final letter inside it

parts.note: a favour is a token of love, as worn by a knight

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word playful is used

parts.note: the word playful supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: A token of affection includes a playful slap at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Smack is not a hit here but a taste, as in 'smacks of garlic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a slight taste or tinge, so it means flavour.

clue.text: Such, if replanted, will lead to a blossom

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come before the single letter
planted again elsewhere, so these letters move into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: replant such a thing and it will flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuchsia is a shrub with drooping pink and purple flowers.

clue.text: Frighten one away from person following regime

indicators.note: the letter for one is taken out of the dieting word

parts.note: a dieter follows a diet regime

explanation.surface: Scaring someone off from a person who follows a regime.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage through fear of consequences.

clue.text: Rhubarb served up with American donut

indicators.note: in a down clue the nonsense word is sent upward, reading backwards

parts.note: rhubarb and rot both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: Rhubarb dished up with an American doughnut.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is the mathematical ring-shaped surface, the shape of a ring doughnut.

clue.text: Fool entering shot with old artist

indicators.note: the fool word goes in between the photograph word and the old abbreviation

parts.note: a pic is a photo
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool gets into a photo with an old painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism.

clue.text: Cat lady's limitations? One will abandon nothing

indicators.note: limits are edges, so only the first and last letters of lady are used

parts.note: the word lady; the 's links it to what follows

indicators.note: the letter for one leaves the word for nothing

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A cat lady's shortcomings, one being that she won't give up anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears and a short tail.

clue.text: Leading figure to make small point in front of our group's historian

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come ahead of the pronoun

parts.note: a hero is the principal character
to dot is to mark with a small point
us is our group; the 's links it to what follows

explanation.surface: A leading figure makes a minor point before a historian's group.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodotus, the ancient Greek writer, is called the Father of History.

clue.text: Mockery and a lot of anger over US city

indicators.note: most but not all of the anger word is used

parts.note: ire is anger
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Ridicule and fury aimed at an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is a form of sarcastic or mocking expression that says the opposite of what is meant.

clue.text: Succeed in love, though not in accepting love

indicators.note: the three letters made inside the brackets are excluded from the word for love

parts.note: passion is strong love

indicators.note: the word in takes the zero inside it

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Winning at romance, though failing to accept romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Love does two jobs: passion first, then the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass an exam or test is to succeed in it.

clue.text: Fine, perhaps, to fight where shootout occurs?

parts.note: a fine is one example of a penalty
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A fine might be due for brawling at a gunfight.
explanation.walkthrough: Shootout suggests a Western gunfight, but in football a penalty shootout takes place in this area.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the penalty area, or box, is where spot kicks in a shootout are taken.
